research_question: Does attention residue suggest an actionable free return note and does any Inspire3 product have independent proof of fixing that specific outcome?

sources.scope: two experiments on task transitions; no consumer audio trial
four interruption studies, ready-to-resume method, measured interrupting task
study counts 202 professionals survey and 66/44 student intervention groups; original task return untested
59 publications Zeigarnik and Ovsiankina; memory recall and resumption not attention-residue proxies
specific standard seller offer, 12 levels 48 MP3, session duration and seller performance claims
seller newsletter receipt condition for free audio; distinct from Jetpack
Total Focus recording feature and claims; product efficacy not established
14-day policy max five refunded sessions yearly; no refund fulfillment proof
Focus Shot marketed contents, not effectiveness
111 RCTs 9538 participants explicitly excluded one-session; no Zen12 proof
five studies n277; pooled state-anxiety k3 n100 low certainty, high bias
material relationships and adjacent clear disclosures
